summary: Peirous or Peiroos (Ancient Greek: Πείροος) is named in Homer's Catalogue of Ships as co-captain, with Acamas, of the Thracians whom the strong stream of the Hellespont encloses. Later books of the Iliad tell the battlefield career of Peiros son of Imbrasus from Aenus under a closely related spelling; the atlas stores the Catalogue captain and the battlefield captain as linked but separate nodes.

sections.heading: Catalogue Thracian
paragraphs: Iliad 2.844–850 places Acamas and Peirous as leaders of the Thracians from across the Hellespont. The Catalogue gives no patronym or city for Peirous alone; the fuller narrative of a Thracian from Aenus who slays Diores and falls to Thoas of Aetolia uses the spelling Peiros and names Imbrasus as father.

Wikipedia unifies the Homeric spellings on one page. Many readers treat Catalogue Peirous and battlefield Peiros as one figure; the atlas keeps peirous-thracian as the Catalogue co-captain beside acamas-thracian.

sections.heading: Homonyms and spelling
paragraphs: This atlas entry (peirous-thracian) is the Catalogue captain. Distinct from peiros-thracian (Imbrasus' son slain by Thoas) if the two spellings are read as separate nodes, and from the Achaean river Peiros in the Peloponnese.
